The GENX 1B70 engine is used as the propulsion system for aircraft like the Boeing 747 and Boeing 787-8.
The thermal value (FHV) of hydrogen fuel is 134.778 MJ/kg, while for JP10 and natural gas it is 44.921 MJ/kg and 55.168 MJ/kg respectively.
With a 20°C reduction in inlet air temperature, the engine's thermal efficiency increases by 1.85% and the entropy generation rate decreases by 16.51%.
The nitrogen oxide emission index (SNOx) is calculated as a function of the combustor exit pressure, temperature, and the ratio of liquid water to air.
The exergetic efficiency of the fan, compressor, turbine, and combustor are calculated as the ratio of output exergy to input exergy minus the component's power consumption.
The genetic algorithm optimization was performed with three separate objective functions: thrust maximization, thermal efficiency maximization, and propulsive efficiency maximization.
For the optimal cycle selected based on the economic approach, the entropy generation rate increased by 18.89% and NOx emissions increased by 10.01% compared to the base engine.
For the optimal cycle selected based on the exero-environmental approach, the entropy generation rate decreased by 54.03% and NOx emissions decreased by 42.02% compared to the base engine.
The GENX 1B70 engine has a fan pressure ratio of 1.5, low-pressure compressor pressure ratio of 1.3, high-pressure compressor pressure ratio of 23, and a bypass ratio of 9.1.
Compared to the base engine with JP10 fuel, the optimized cycle with hydrogen fuel showed a 2.65% increase in thermal efficiency.
The TOPSIS method was used to select the best optimized cycles from the Pareto front based on economic and exero-environmental approaches.
Previous studies on turbofan engine optimization focused on lower bypass ratio mixed flow engines, whereas this study analyzes the high-bypass unmixed flow GENX 1B70 engine.
The genetic algorithm optimization involved five main phases: initial population, fitness function, selection, crossover, and mutation.
The thrust-specific fuel consumption (TSFC) of the engine decreased by 2.15% with a 20°C reduction in inlet air temperature.
The nitrogen oxide emission index (SNOx) is an important parameter that indicates the environmental impact of the engine.
